summary: A red flashing light on the breakwater at Gimli, Manitoba, on Lake Winnipeg. The 1910 pier lighthouse's lantern room now sits on a 1973 replica by the waterfront.

structures.note: A 23-foot square wooden tower with a square wooden lantern, erected 1910 on the pier. Moved in 1912. Pushed over by ice in April 1943. The sources do not say what became of this tower.

Replica tower that carries the original 1910 lantern room, in the fishing-village area by the waterfront (MHS). LighthouseFriends places it near the foot of the pier, attached to the Lake Winnipeg Visitor Centre and harbour master buildings.
Square skeleton tower with a red and white rectangular daymark at the outer end of the breakwater (CCG List of Lights, entry 1569).

staffing.note: Keepers are named to at least 1946 (LighthouseFriends). The sources do not say when keeping ended.

access.note: The Gimli waterfront. The sources do not say whether the breakwater is open to walkers.

visit.note: The replica tower is in the fishing-village area and is run as a tourist attraction (MHS). The lighthouse can be seen along the waterfront (LighthouseFriends).

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (the light); New Iceland Heritage Museum (the replica tower and lantern room, per MHS)

events.note: First permanent pier built with federal help, by the Icelandic contractor J.J. Vopni at a cost of $9,000.
Lighthouse added to the pier: a 23-foot wooden tower with a fifth-order 360-degree lens and a duplex lamp.
Moved to the outer end of a new extension of the pier.
An ice pile-up in April pushed the lighthouse over and damaged it.
Original lantern room set atop a replica tower.

keepers.name: E. G. Thomson
keepers.note: First keeper, hired 1910 at an annual salary of $80 (LighthouseFriends). The Marine report's keeper table spells the name E.G.Thompson, appointed 21 January 1910 at $80 (checked on the page image).

keepers.name: K. Samundsson
keepers.note: Replaced Thomson in 1912 (LighthouseFriends, which gives the span as 1912 to at least 1923). Keeper tables spell the name K. Samundsson and K. Samunds.son. Appointment dated 9 April 1912 in the table for the year ending March 1913 and again in the table for the year ending March 1914 (both checked on the page images).

keepers.name: Pete Thompson
keepers.note: LighthouseFriends gives the span as 1933 to at least 1946, as keeper in the 1930s and 1940s. Also worked as a scaler at the Armstrong-Gimli fish processing plant.

wrecks.outcome: Total wreck. Caught by a northeast gale while lying at the dock at Gimli, and pounded against the dock. This was before the 1910 lighthouse was built.

corrections.why: The record's position is the CCG List of Lights entry 1570, Gimli Harbour, a separate private aid on the same breakwater end. The light whose characteristic the record uses (entry 1569, Gimli, Fl R 4s, 7.7 m, 5 nm) is at 50 37 44.9 N, 096 58 51.1 W, about 70 m away. A reviewer should confirm which light the record describes.

notes_for_editor: Moderate station: four chapters. Keepers: E. G. Thomson (1910 to 1912), K. Samundsson (1912 to at least 1923), Pete Thompson (1933 to at least 1946). Thomson and Samundsson appear in the Marine keeper tables (OCR) and in LighthouseFriends. The page images were checked on 2026-10-28: FY1911 printed p. 249 (scan 256), FY1913 printed p. 78 (scan 85), FY1914 printed p. 70 (scan 77); each Gimli row was read against its neighbours. The FY1913 salary of $80 was read from the image and is not legible in the OCR, so the story does not rely on it. The LighthouseFriends dates agree with the tables. Thompson's span (1933 to 1946) rests on LighthouseFriends alone: the corpus Marine reports end in 1924. Disagreement: the federal grant year is 1899 in the Manitoba Historical Society text and 1898 in LighthouseFriends; the story gives both and does not choose. The 1912 move and the Buchanan & Fraser payment rest on LighthouseFriends only; a Marine report table for the year ending March 1913 lists Buchanan & Fraser as a contractor on a different line, and it was not matched to Gimli. The CCG list was checked on 2026-10-28: entry 1569 is Gimli (Fl R 4s, focal height 7.7 m, nominal range 5 nm, square skeleton tower); entry 1570 Gimli Harbour is a separate private aid (Fl G 4s, 50 37 45.5 N, 096 58 54.7 W), which the record's position matches (see corrections). LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: facts paraphrased, one short quotation at most. Not used: Wikipedia, MarineRadar (an aggregator that repeats the Manitoba Historical Society), and a Facebook post on the 1943 ice damage. Newspapers were not searched: Chronicling America holds US papers only. Photos: the Manitoba Historical Society page shows photographs from the Archives of Manitoba (Loudon G. Wilson fonds, PR1978-14, photo 198, circa 1910-1917) and from two contributors (2017, 2024), with no licence stated; none were added. Keep the current light (entry 1569) separate from the 1910 light in any page structure: the current light is a skeleton tower at the breakwater end; the 1910 lantern room sits on a 1973 replica.
